correctness.rationale: Quantification is over Boolean valuations of one letter at one root of a loopless undirected cycle, with depths 1 through n-1 indexed syntactically. The endpoint support B_j consists of j-2t modulo n for 0 <= t <= j. For any positive set, the valuation equal to its support union satisfies every negative whose support is not contained in that union. Consequently a minimal obstruction has exactly one negative, with pairs exactly the single-support containments; two positives of the same parity would make the smaller redundant. In even order the two parity chains lie on disjoint shores. In odd order n=2r+1 supports have size j+1 up to n-1; at e+o=n-2 for opposite-parity depths they are disjoint (opposite-parity integer endpoints could coincide modulo n only if separated by at least n) and partition the cycle. Nested enlargement gives the same cover above the threshold. Below it, a negative depth exceeding the same-parity positive by at least two has a new endpoint e+2 or o+2 absent from both supports, by distinct same-parity endpoints and the parity-specific walk bound. Once the union covers, the larger negative exceeds its same-parity support and its 0 (even) or 1 (odd) is absent from the opposite support (a full n-1 positive is excluded). This proves both directions. For e=2a, o=2b+1 the condition is a+b >= r-1, with a in 1..r-1 and b in 0..r-1. Each contributes r-a+r-1-b negatives; summing over b first gives (a+1)(2r-a)/2, then r(r-1)(2r+5)/6. At r=1 no a is available. With all depths at most r, the only candidate opposite-parity positives satisfying the threshold are r-1,r and neither can be exceeded by two. For r>=2 the depths r-1,r,r+1 do give a minimal triple. The proof is unrestricted in n; frozen finite checks cover only the documented ranges.
residual_risks: The count is for the finite depth-indexed agenda only, not an infinite agenda with repeated full supports or an arbitrary modal language.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The general cover test is used, not rediscovered as a contribution; deriving the sharp two-parity cover threshold, negative-level exclusions and first admissible depth needs the specific walk geometry. value.rationale: Minimal inconsistency is a motivated obstruction in genuinely modal agendas. Here the classification decides all witnesses on an infinite standard family and reveals exactly how odd-cycle overlap creates a failure of pairwise consistency, including a sharp depth threshold that the numerical sequence alone cannot give. This is valuable as a classification and not merely as the evaluation of the cubic or as a new general aggregation impossibility result.
residual_risks: Consequences beyond the single-letter symmetric-cycle agenda, including any new aggregation theorem, are not established.
